diseases.name: Halo Blight
diseases.description: A bacterial disease of beans with small brown spots inside wide yellow-green halos.
diseases.causes: The bacteria come in on infected seed and spread by rain splash, wind and handling in cool, wet weather.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn brown
A wide yellow-green halo round each spot
Greasy spots on pods; young leaves yellow overall
diseases.effect: Leaves and pods are spotted; yield and seed quality fall.
diseases.untreated: Infected seed carries it into the next crop.

steps.title: Remove badly spotted plants
steps.instruction: Pick off badly spotted plants when the plants are dry and take them away.

steps.title: Stay out of wet crops
steps.instruction: Do not handle or work among wet plants.

steps.title: Copper spray where advised
steps.instruction: Spray a registered copper product following the label.

lifecycle: Brown spots with wide halos form.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: bean halo blight

diseases.name: Bean Common Mosaic
diseases.pathogen: Bean common mosaic virus (BCMV, a potyvirus)
diseases.description: A virus disease that mottles and curls bean leaves.
diseases.causes: Carried in seed and spread by aphids that probe infected plants.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic on the leaves
Leaves puckered, curled down and narrow
diseases.untreated: Infected seed spreads it to the next crop.

steps.title: Remove infected plants early
steps.instruction: Pull out mottled plants while few.

steps.title: Control weeds and aphids
steps.instruction: Keep weeds down round the crop.
steps.rationale: Hosts for aphids and the virus.

steps.title: Use certified seed next time
steps.instruction: Buy virus-free seed of resistant varieties.

lifecycle: Seed from infected plants carries it.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: bean mosaic virus
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Bean Rust
diseases.description: A rust fungus of bean leaves.
diseases.causes: Spores blow in on the wind or survive on old bean debris; leaves wet for 10+ hours in mild weather get infected.
symptoms: Small white flecks that become rusty red-brown pustules
Pustules often ringed by a yellow halo
Heavily infected leaves yellow and drop
diseases.untreated: Severe early rust can cut yield substantially.

steps.title: Remove rusted leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off rusted leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Space plants and avoid evening watering
Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores survive on debris or blow in.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: bean rust
